PullRequest.Title: sessions: Show status indicators in collapsed sections
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- Add `sessions.list.showUnreadInCollapsedSections`, disabled by default with automatic experiment control.
- Replace collapsed group/workspace icons using this priority among the sessions they actually contain:
  1. Needs input: the existing orange ring pixel spinner.
  2. Failing CI while the session is not in progress: an orange dot, using the existing blocked-session CI model.
  3. Unread: the existing blue dot.
- Archived sessions never contribute any of these indicators. Group membership, filters, pin/archive precedence, and sessions behind Show More are respected; a session displayed only in a custom group does not mark its underlying workspace.
- Preserve chevrons on hover and keyboard focus, restore normal icons when expanded, and react to CI, status, read-state, archive, and setting changes.
- Expose status in accessible header labels and preserve the existing reduced-motion fallback. Automations behavior remains unchanged.

## Validation
- Client compilation and TypeScript checking passed with zero errors.
- 141 focused unit tests passed, covering session-list behavior, configuration registration, and the underlying blocked-session CI model.
- 25 Playwright scenarios validated across dark, light, and both high-contrast themes, covering all three indicators, ownership, hover, expansion/collapse, keyboard focus, and the default-disabled setting. Local page-load timeouts passed on focused reruns; one rerun used a 60-second local test timeout without changing committed test timeouts.
- Hygiene/lint and source-layer checks passed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed constructor path, lazy activation through the consumed `sessionsWithFailingCI` observable, and `BlockedSessions` implementation were traced directly. Its `_allSessions` and per-session observables drive a full loop, PR/CI reference acquisition, and sort on recomputation. Existing reference collections coalesce network models, so the regression is CPU/allocation rather than duplicate requests; exact delay depends on session-history size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and transient objects/references created while scanning sessions and aggregating blocked CI state
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each relevant update adds O(N + P + B log B) work for N managed sessions, P sessions with pull requests/CI references, and B blocked sessions, even though an equivalent workbench-owned blocked-session computation is already live.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased UI-thread CPU/GC pressure and slower Sessions-list updates
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, constructing/rendering `SessionsList` did not create another `BlockedSessions`; blocked-state collection-wide work was performed by existing workbench owners only, and the list had no duplicate full-history aggregation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Opening the Sessions view with the setting enabled now activates an additional independent blocked-session derivation. On every management-session event or observed status/archive/PR/CI change, that derivation walks the complete session collection, reacquires shared PR/CI references for applicable sessions, sorts blocked results, and then allocates filter/map arrays plus a new failing-CI `Set`.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line constructs a fresh `BlockedSessions` inside every `SessionsList` when the experiment is enabled (`reader.store.add(instantiationService.createInstance(BlockedSessions))`), rather than reusing the already workbench-owned model created by `SessionsTitleBarContribution` (and, on desktop, `SessionsApplicationBadge`).
Findings.Title: Reuse the existing blocked-session aggregation
Findings.Impact: With the experiment enabled and the Sessions view open, users with long agent-session histories pay a second collection-wide pass and transient reference/array allocation for routine session updates and CI polling changes, increasing UI-thread CPU/GC pressure and delaying list reactions.
Findings.Evidence: `BlockedSessions.blockedSessionsWithReasons` iterates every `ISessionsManagementService.getSessions()` entry, calls `_getBlockedSession` (including shared PR and CI reference acquisition), and sorts the blocked array. This work is already owned at workbench scope by `SessionsTitleBarContribution` from BlockRestore (and by the application badge on desktop), but the new list-local instance cannot reuse that computation. Agent-host providers emit session-change events for read, archive, title, summary, and notification updates, so the duplicate pass is not limited to initial render.
Findings.Recommendation: Provide one shared workbench/service-owned `BlockedSessions` (or shared failing-CI observable) to the list and reference-count only the list subscription while the setting is enabled, instead of constructing an independent model per list.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and use the Sessions view while collapsed-section indicators remain disabled (the default).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList construction and visible header rendering are synchronous on the UI thread. The new observables short-circuit on the false configuration value, so blocked-session aggregation and per-session status scans do not enter the critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently rendered section/group headers; virtualized templates bound the live header count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI construction and autoruns run synchronously; no new queue, limiter, or concurrent work is activated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The blocked-session derived remains cold and creates no model; PR/CI reference caches are untouched by this diff path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: short-circuit dependency order and observable activation are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only small fixed observable/autorun setup is added per rendered header; no realistic scaling regression was established while disabled.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Sessions view with the experiment enabled and consume failing-CI indicators.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial blocked-state consumption and subsequent session/status/archive/PR/CI updates synchronously recompute the new list-local BlockedSessions model before reactive header/ARIA consumers settle. GitHub fetches remain asynchronous and are not newly required for view progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh and poll pull-request and CI state through GitHub API fetchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing polling performs PR refreshes per tracked pull request and CI refreshes per open non-draft PR, generally every 60 seconds; shared model keys coalesce consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The after-restored polling contribution already acquired, refreshed, and polled these shared models before the PR; the added list model only adds references and duplicate CPU aggregation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the Sessions-list render critical path; list indicators consume the resulting observables asynchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N managed sessions, P sessions carrying PR data, and B blocked sessions; cost is O(N + P + B log B) per relevant update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Blocked-state derivations are synchronous and independently duplicate the existing workbench-owned derivation. Existing per-PR network polling remains concurrent and unchanged; ReferenceCollection coalesces models by PR/head key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold list activation acquires shared PR/CI model references; warm models are reused by owner/repo/PR/head keys. No additional network fetch is caused by acquisition itself, but each recompute allocates new reference handles, arrays, and a Set. Disabling the setting disposes the list-local model and its references.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line creates an independent model, and the model implementation loops all sessions, reacquires references, sorts, and is already instantiated by workbench-level owners.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on managed-session and PR counts, but the duplicate full-collection mechanism and update reachability are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium repeated-work regression; one finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse/expand sections and process read, status, archive, membership, or filter changes with indicators enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collapse toggles and reactive session changes synchronously derive a section status and update one visible header icon/ARIA label. Status aggregation includes sessions behind Show More by design.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of sessions in the affected section, including hidden Show More entries, plus the number of visible collapsed headers whose CI-set dependency changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable recomputation and DOM updates are serialized on the UI thread; no coalescing beyond derived-value equality, and no external boundary is crossed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Header status is derived and primitive-equality suppresses unchanged DOM rerenders. SessionStatusIcon instances retain a spinner only while the corresponding header status is active and are disposed through the row element store.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-section linear scans and bounded visible DOM ownership; uncertain that this incremental cost alone crosses the reporting threshold.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large single groups can make scans noticeable, but each session belongs to one effective rendered section after custom-group/pin/archive placement, and no separate high-confidence regression beyond the duplicate global aggregation was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional bounded UI work for the feature; omitted as a separate finding to avoid duplicating the reported aggregation cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the collapsed-section indicator setting at runtime.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enabling synchronously activates and initially computes the list-local blocked-session model; disabling disposes it and restores normal icons. Configuration persistence itself is outside the changed implementation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential PR/CI model refreshes are owned by the pre-existing polling contribution, not by reference acquisition during the toggle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No new requests per toggle; references are shared by stable keys and the polling cadence remains per PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Toggling this new setting did not exist; existing GitHub polling continued independently of Sessions-list configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network is off the toggle critical path; synchronous full-session recomputation is the relevant cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Managed-session and PR counts at enable time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Setting notifications serialize reactive teardown/recreation; no overlapping list-local models survive disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared ReferenceCollection entries survive when held by existing workbench pollers/indicators; otherwise disposal can release them. There is no negative-cache behavior introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for deterministic model creation/disposal and shared cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated manual toggling is uncommon; the meaningful trigger is experiment enablement followed by normal session updates.
Scenarios.Verdict: The activation cost is covered by the submitted repeated-work finding; no separate lifecycle finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff pages. Traced UI rendering, observable ownership, blocked-session aggregation, GitHub model references/polling, configuration toggles, accessibility updates, cache sharing, and disposal. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence repeated-work finding for the list-local duplicate BlockedSessions aggregation; no new network fan-out or cleanup leak was established.
